context: Tests whether the agent implements Bearer Token JWT authentication middleware with correct HTTP status codes on failure and secure logging that never exposes raw token values in error responses or log output.

checklist.name: Bearer scheme required
checklist.description: Middleware validates the Authorization header uses the 'Bearer' scheme (checks for 'Bearer ' prefix or equivalent, not just any Authorization header value)

checklist.name: JWT format validation
checklist.description: Middleware verifies the token is a properly structured JWT — three base64url-encoded segments separated by dots (header.payload.signature)

checklist.name: Signature verification
checklist.description: Middleware verifies the JWT signature against a secret or public key (e.g. calls jwt.verify() or equivalent, not just jwt.decode())

checklist.name: Expiry check
checklist.description: Middleware checks that the token has not expired (validates the 'exp' claim or equivalent)

checklist.name: Missing token → 401
checklist.description: Returns HTTP status 401 when the Authorization header is absent from the request

checklist.name: Malformed token → 401
checklist.description: Returns HTTP status 401 when the token is present but structurally invalid or fails signature verification

checklist.name: Expired token → 401
checklist.description: Returns HTTP status 401 when the token has a valid structure and signature but has expired

checklist.name: Token absent from error body
checklist.description: Error response body does NOT include the raw token string value — the response body contains only generic error descriptions (e.g. 'Unauthorized', 'Invalid token') without interpolating the actual token

checklist.name: Token absent from log output
checklist.description: Log statements for authentication failures do NOT include the raw token value — log calls use generic messages, error type, or redacted placeholders rather than interpolating the credential string

checklist.name: README example present
checklist.description: middleware/README.md includes a concrete example showing both the error response body format and a sample failed-authentication log line
